mentions.name: RF monitoring system
mentions.description: This system monitors RF spectrum via BT/BLE/WiFi sensors on low-power hardware like a Raspberry Pi, correlating device sightings to report events such as a parked car coinciding with a known Bluetooth device. It alerts on sudden cross-spectrum disturbances (e.g. burglars using a cheap jammer to disable WiFi cameras) and on known devices losing contact or leaving premises, and supports multiple listening pods to review device movement across a campus or neighborhood. It provides a web UI, can publish events to an external security system, and is gaining an LLM interface so non-technical operators can set policies and ask questions about events. It could be sold as an appliance or as a license for a DIY build.
mentions.problem: Detecting security events such as intruders using cheap jammers to disable WiFi cameras and known devices losing contact or leaving premises.
mentions.audience: Non-technical operators who set policies and query events; sold as an appliance or a license for a DIY build.
mentions.source_excerpt:
I'm building an RF monitoring system.

It can tell you things like:

- The car that parked nearby last night coincided with a "Derek's Galaxy Buds" device with MAC address aa:bb:cc:dd:ee:ff. The buds also drove by briefly the previous night.

- Alert on sudden cross-specturm disturbance (e.g. burglars using a cheap jammer to disable WiFi cameras).

- Alert on known device contact loss (powered off / left premises).

- Review device movement across a campus/neighborhood (using multiple listening pods).

I have a working PoC. It can run on a cheap, low-power computer (e.g. Raspberry Pi) supporting multiple RF sensors (BT/BLE/WiFi). Has a web UI. Can publish events to an external security system. Currently working on an LLM interface to make it trivial for a non-technical operator to set policies and ask questions about events.

Could be sold as an appliance or a license for a DIY build.

Seed investors are welcome to contact rf-monitor@tuta.com
